text_plugin_synopsis: Offline speech recognition, wake word detection, voice activity detection and neural text-to-speech, usable as the system TTS engine

p_build_intro: This section targets developers who want to build the plugin from source.
p_roadmap: Plans, design decisions and progress are tracked as a checklist in ROADMAP.md. Unchecked items are plans, not features of the current version.
p_introduction_what: 3-Macaw Speech uses [sherpa-onnx]({{ sherpa_onnx_url }}) to run speech recognition, voice activity detection, wake word detection and neural text-to-speech offline on the device. Everything is computed locally and no audio is uploaded.
p_introduction_how: The plugin is a separately installed APK. AutoJs6 scripts use it through the global `speech` module; the speech synthesis also registers as an Android system TTS engine, so the AutoJs6 `tts` module and other apps can choose it. Recognition and synthesis models are not bundled with the APK but downloaded on demand from the plugin screen or a script; only the voice activity detection model is built in.
p_status_note: This is a development preview: AutoJs6 can discover the plugin, which downloads and manages models, recognizes speech, detects voice activity and wake words, and synthesizes speech, also as the system TTS engine; its own screens manage the models, try them out and hold the settings. The AutoJs6 version that provides the `speech` script module is not released yet. The text below describes the 1.0.0 design; see the roadmap for the progress.
features: Speech recognition: streaming dictation from the microphone (partial and final results in real time) and WAV file recognition, with offline models for Chinese, English, mixed Chinese and English, Japanese, Korean and Cantonese.
Voice activity detection: the built-in silero VAD v5 splits audio into speech segments on its own and also ends dictation sentences automatically.
Wake words: type the keyword as plain text (for example `小六小六` or `hey macaw`) without training a model; after waking up, dictation can start automatically.
Text-to-speech: several neural Chinese and English voices, synthesized to WAV files or used as the system TTS engine by the AutoJs6 `tts` module and other apps.
System voice input: microphone buttons in other apps, such as 3-Stove Agent, can use the offline recognition; you say one sentence in a bottom sheet and the recognized text goes back to that app.

Digital assistant: choose 3-Macaw Speech as the default digital assistant app, then long press the power or Home button, say one sentence, edit the recognized text if needed and hand it to 3-Stove Agent, 3-Stone AI or another app that takes voice commands, or copy it; as the assistant it is also the speech recognition service other apps use.

Model management: downloads from a signed model catalog, enabled only after every file passes its SHA-256 check, plus import of local models; models restricted to non-commercial use show their license before the download.
usage_steps: Update AutoJs6 to internal build {{ required_host_version_code }} ({{ required_host_version_name }}) or later.
Download the APK that matches the device ABI from [Releases]({{ repo_url }}/releases) (choose `universal` if unsure) and install it, then authorize and enable it in the AutoJs6 Plugin Center.
Open the plugin screen to grant the microphone permission and download the models you need, then use the `speech` module in scripts.
p_usage_note: The plugin supports devices running Android {{ min_android_version }} (API {{ android_min_sdk }}) or later. There is one package per ABI and a `universal` package for every device.
p_models_intro: Recognition, wake word and synthesis models take 30 MB to 350 MB each, so they are not bundled with the APK. The plugin downloads them from immutable releases of the AutoJs6 shared assets repository and falls back to the upstream sherpa-onnx address when the mirror is unavailable; on both paths every file must pass its SHA-256 check before the model is enabled.
p_models_license: Every model carries its license. Models restricted to non-commercial use (for example a synthesis model trained on the DataBaker corpus) show a notice before the download, and scripts must pass `acceptLicense: true` explicitly.
p_script_api_intro: Scripts use these capabilities through the global `speech` module (also available as `$speech`; this is the 1.0.0 design draft, the documentation of the released version prevails)
api_points: `speech.listen(options)` opens a dictation session that reports results through events such as `partial`, `final` and `end`; `speech.recognize(path)` recognizes a WAV file.
`speech.wake(keywords, options)` opens a wake word session; `thenListen` starts dictation automatically after a wake up.
`speech.synthesize(text, path)` synthesizes to a WAV file; `speech.speak(text)` and `tts(text, {engine})` speak through the system TTS engine; `speech.models` manages the models.

faq.q: Do recognition and synthesis need the Internet?
faq.a: No. Once the models are downloaded, everything runs on the device and no audio is uploaded. The plugin only goes online to download models and refresh the model catalog.

faq.q: Why does the plugin request the microphone permission itself?
faq.a: Audio is recorded inside the plugin process and never passes through AutoJs6. AutoJs6 hands its foreground capabilities to the plugin when it binds, and the plugin holds a microphone foreground service during a microphone session, so dictation goes on after AutoJs6 moves to the background or the screen turns off. Grant the microphone permission on the plugin screen before the first use.
Most phones need `arm64-v8a`. If you are unsure about the device ABI, install `universal`: it works on every device but is larger.

faq.q: How do I use 3-Macaw Speech as the text-to-speech engine of the system?
faq.a: Install at least one synthesis model first, then choose 3-Macaw Speech as the preferred engine in the text-to-speech settings of the system (usually under Accessibility or Languages). Every speaker of a model is a voice named `<model id>/<speaker number>`; bilingual models also offer `<model id>/<speaker number>/en-US` for English. AutoJs6 scripts can pick the engine without changing the system setting: `tts(text, {engine: "io.github.supermonster003.autojs6.plugin.three.macaw.speech"})` or `speech.speak(text)`.

faq.q: Can other apps use 3-Macaw Speech for voice input?
faq.a: Yes. With a recognition model installed and the microphone permission granted, apps that start the system voice input (for example the microphone button of 3-Stove Agent) open the 3-Macaw Speech sheet. If another voice input app such as Google is installed, Android asks which one to use and can remember the choice. To hide the entry from other apps, turn off 'Use as the system voice input' in the recognition group of the settings.

faq.q: How do I make 3-Macaw Speech the default digital assistant?
faq.a: Open the settings of 3-Macaw Speech and tap Digital assistant in the recognition group: the system settings open, where you choose 3-Macaw Speech as the digital assistant app (the page may be named a little differently on some systems). Then long press the power or Home button, or use the assist gesture, to dictate. If the power button is set to another function on your phone, use the Home button or the assist gesture.

faq.q: Why does the assistant not listen for a wake word all the time?
faq.a: Listening all the time keeps the microphone, an ongoing notification and the microphone indicator on and uses more battery, so the digital assistant listens only when you press the assist button. Apps such as 3-Stone AI and 3-Stove Agent can offer their own always-on listening switch (off by default); while one listens, the digital assistant, voice input and speech recognition still work, and wake word detection pauses and resumes by itself afterwards. A built-in wake word of 3-Macaw Speech itself is planned for a later version.

p_security_intro: The plugin keeps its permission surface as small as possible:
security_points: Microphone: audio is recorded only for dictation, wake words and the tryout screen, and the microphone is released as soon as the session ends or the script exits.
Network: used only to download models and refresh the signed model catalog; recognition and synthesis stay offline.
Storage: models live in the private directory of the plugin and local models are imported through the system file picker, so no storage permission is requested.

Protected entries: the capability service and the activation entry require the AutoJs6 plugin permission (`org.autojs.permission.PLUGIN`), so other apps cannot call them directly; the system TTS engine and its voice check, sample text and settings entries are open to every app, as Android requires, and only synthesize speech.

System voice input: like the system TTS engine it is open to every app; it records only while its sheet is on the screen, returns nothing but the recognized text and can be turned off in the settings.

Digital assistant: it never reads the screen and does not listen in the background; it records only while its sheet is on the screen, and the recognized text leaves the sheet only when you tap an app button or copy it (on the lock screen, after you unlock). The speech recognition service recognizes only for apps that hold the microphone permission themselves.
